overview: This one-page file register concerns Japanese legal requirements for ships’ officers in 1932. It records a May 2 paper from Hill at Yokohama summarizing or quoting Japanese law and noting that no additional regulations specified vessel manning scales, while directing readers to decimal-file reference 800.866/62 for related material.

subfiles.title: List of papers concerning ships’ officers in Japan
subfiles.about: The register records a paper concerning Japanese law governing ships’ officers and vessel manning scales.
subfiles.summary: This list-of-papers sheet describes a May 2, 1932 submission from Hill at Yokohama containing quotations from Japanese law on ships’ officers. The entry states that Japanese law specified no other regulations concerning vessel manning scales. It cross-references related material filed under 800.866/62.

interest: The page is useful chiefly as archival metadata: it documents a now-absent or separately filed communication about Japanese maritime crewing law and supplies the sender, date, subject, and a related decimal-file reference. For historians of maritime labor or regulation, its most notable claim is that the cited Japanese law imposed no further vessel manning-scale requirements. The cross-reference to 800.866/62 may help reconstruct the broader documentary trail.
